mediastinal lymph nodes and fat.notes: Yellow/orange fatty tissue held and lifted by graspers = the node/fat block being dissected. High confidence in shot C2 (frames 175, 192: clearly yellow lobulated fat pulled toward the top right); medium in B (frame 110: small orange piece between grasper jaws, vapour around it) and C3 (frame 256: glistening orange cut tissue edge held by two instruments at the right, partly pleura edge). Probably also present but not identifiable with confidence in A1, A2 (at the instrument tips), C1 (top of the cavity) and C4 (orange fibrous tissue inside the incision channel); not seen in D (likely removed). Its appearance changes between shots (different pieces of the block), so each prompt is per shot.

mediastinal pleura.notes: Prompted only where it is unambiguous: in shots C4 and D, the intact, translucent membrane with fine surface vessels lying over yellow mediastinal fat to the right of the incision/dissection beds. The mask is the pleura-plus-fat surface (depth = the fat under it); the fat under it may be part of the node block or loose fat - not separable. In shots A2-C3 the smooth pale band arching above the cavity is bounded by what looks like the cut pleural edge, but what lies under it (fat, azygos, SVC or trachea) is unclear, so it was not prompted.

dissection bed.notes: ADDED. Raw, blood-stained tissue surface exposed by the dissection (the cavity left after node/fat removal). High confidence in A2, C1, C2, C3 (the central red cavity); medium in D (two dark-red raw beds) and C4 (the opened pleural incision channel, raw fat/node tissue being divided). Blood staining is included here; there is no separate pool of blood to segment. Present but unprompted in A1 (blurred close-up) and B/B2 (hidden by instruments and vapour).

white curved cord.notes: ADDED. Smooth white glistening cord about 8-15 px wide, curved like a C/J with a hooked upper end, lying on the left side of the cavity in shots A2, B2, C1, C2, C3. It is easy to segment (high mask confidence), but what it is remains unknown (most likely a nerve, e.g. the vagus, left in place; possibly exposed cartilage). Do not give it vessel or airway properties. It is a stable, rigid-looking landmark in 5 of 9 shots, which is why it is worth tracking. Absent in C4; possibly the pale curve at the far left of shot D (not prompted).
